newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps rates $1-bln Mexican bond issue BB.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps rates $1-bln Mexican bond issue BB.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said it assigned a foreign currency rating of double-B, or "BB," to a $1-billion Mexican global bond issue due 2016.

"The Mexican government's commitment to tight monetary and fiscal policies has caused annual inflation to steadily decline from 52 percent at the end of 1995 to 31.8 percent in June 1996," said the credit rating firm.
Duff & Phelps said GDP growth has resumed and may reach the three percent official estimate for 1996.

"Real interest rates have decreased and confidence is gradually returning. Net capital inflows and a practically balanced current account allowed international reserves to recover from $6.1 billion at year-end to $15.8 billion in June 1996 and stabilized the peso," the firm said.
"The ailing financial sector remains a concern, but has benefitted from improving fundamentals as well as a restructuring program," Duff & Phelps said.

The country's financial position is backed by strong direct foreign investment, the firm said, adding "international capital flows ... will continue to be crucial in complementing Mexico's low domestic savings."
